answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. Consider a delta as the anchor of the cost.
